cold_context: Only the three supplied criteria files and rendered PDF were read. No source, packet, manifest, research notes or prior reviews consulted. All 30 pages rendered with PyMuPDF at 1.3x and visually inspected individually.

findings.finding: “We partly replicated Schwabe’s (2016) finding that psychometric modelling improves behavioural-genetic inference” leads with source and composite verdict. The same abstract immediately limits precision results, empirical refits, Bayesian recovery, power, bias reversals and mathematical uniqueness.

Opening partly-replicated verdict precedes motivation; 108 precision comparisons are distinguished from power, empirical application and Bayesian recovery. Two numerical illustrations and 11 unsupported bias reversals follow immediately.

The manuscript defines its scientific question and source without prior-draft dependence. Sections 3–7 explain results and assumptions; Appendix A states headline propositions and assessments. Visible spacing and raw identifiers impede polish in sections 8/10 and Appendix A but do not require previous conversation to interpret.

findings.location: Abstract and overview table; Appendix A pp13–21
findings.finding: The rendered paper presents 26 principal headline rows plus two scalar illustrations and explicitly separates partial, blocked and unresolved conclusions. External fidelity to the dissertation must await the authorized source pass.

findings.location: Appendix B, coverage introduction and table pp21–22
findings.finding: The PDF declares 996 dependent inventory records, 26 headlines, 187 signed components, and chapter/appendix coverage. The 187 component rows are visibly retained on pp22–27. Completeness against the packet cannot yet be verified.

The fourteen explicit limitations preserve unavailable inputs, reconstruction assumptions, single-dataset posterior limits, source uncertainty, multiplicity, missing power, no formal certificates, dependence and incomplete score chains. Whether every packet limitation is faithfully retained remains unverified.

findings.location: Sections 5.3 and 6; Appendix C p27 and D pp28–29
findings.finding: Incomplete exact-score workload is not called scientific replication; source-only empirical arithmetic is not a refit. Rebuilding and source generation are distinguished on p27, and process compliance is explicitly not scientific validation on p28.

Abstract names and cites Schwabe (2016); p2 and p30 supply dissertation title and University of Twente. Exact identity and original finding must be checked against the actual source after cold record is saved.

findings.location: Overview table and note; sections3.1–3.2 pp3–4; AppendixB pp22–27
findings.finding: Effect magnitude and direction are separately displayed. HE27 shows 0.00106356 versus 0.00150235, same direction but not-established magnitude; HE28 shows 0.03315402 versus 0.03118039, smaller with same direction. Caption defines contrasts, units, rounding/extraction bounds and “Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.” Source precision, numerical equality and classifications require packet/source verification.

findings.location: Nonscalar rows and note; Appendix A pp13–21
findings.finding: Nonscalar rows explicitly retain scientific verdicts separately from unavailable aggregate magnitude; Appendix A supplies proposition-specific applicability explanations and AppendixB retains components. Source-supported classification needs verification.
